title: Mild Butter Chicken
subtitle: tender chicken thighs in a creamy, buttery tomato sauce with warm garam masala: all flavour, no heat
imageAlt: Creamy orange butter chicken in a white bowl beside jasmine rice on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Tomato paste, cumin, turmeric, paprika, sugar, salt

beforeYouStart.text: Garam masala is a warm spice blend (cinnamon, cumin, cardamom), not a hot one. There's no chili in this.
Start the rice first; it's ready when the chicken is.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the salt and 1 tsp of the garam masala.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large deep skillet over medium-high. Brown the chicken in 2 batches, 2–3 minutes a side; it doesn't need to cook through. Move to a plate.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining 2 tbsp butter and the onion. Cook 6–7 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste, the remaining 2 tsp garam masala, the cumin, turmeric and paprika and cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in the tomato sauce, sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the cream, then the chicken and its juices. Simmer gently 8–10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the sauce coats a spoon.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Taste for salt and serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: It boiled after the cream went in. Lower the heat and stir in 2–3 tbsp cream or water until smooth.
Simmer uncovered a few minutes more; it thickens as it reduces.
Cook the tomato paste and spices the full minute, and add another pinch of sugar.
It boiled too hard. Keep it at a gentle bubble; thighs stay tender.

saleTip: Boneless thighs at No Frills drop to about $11–13/kg on sale; buy the family pack and freeze in 900 g bags.
swap: Chicken breast: same amount, but simmer only 6–8 minutes in the sauce so it stays juicy. Still 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Even better the next day. Pack with rice for lunch, or wrap in a warm tortilla.
doneness: Chicken pieces at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada). Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested home-style butter chicken (murgh makhani) methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): browned thighs finished in a buttery tomato, garam masala and cream sauce, with the chili left out.
prepAhead: Cut and season the chicken up to 1 day ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
The finished curry keeps 3–4 days and freezes well.
reheat: Covered over medium-low, stirring, with a splash of water, or in the microwave 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Garam masala and paprika only, and no fresh ginger.

stepNotes.3: Basic: skip the ginger, cumin and turmeric.

fancy.note: Warm buttered naan to scoop it up, and a swirl of cream on top.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Warm the naan in a dry skillet 1 minute a side and brush with the melted butter. Swirl the cream over each bowl.

plating: Rice to one side, curry beside it, not on top.
A swirl of cream over the sauce.
Naan cut in triangles, leaning on the bowl.

why.0-0: Thighs stay juicy in the simmer where breast can go dry.
why.1-4: Frying tomato paste and spices in butter deepens the flavour and takes away the raw edge.
why.1-9: A little sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes.

funFact: Butter chicken was created in the 1950s at Moti Mahal in Delhi, to use up leftover tandoori chicken in a buttery tomato gravy.

keeps.note: freeze the curry without the rice

pairs: fried rice instead of plain for a takeout night
